title: Enforce response_contract with strict-mode and streaming safety for structured outputs
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers consuming structured outputs (response_format / response_contract) reported subtle inconsistencies when streaming partial tokens or when tool/function-calling pipes through the OpenAI compatibility layer. This PR introduces a first-class 'response_contract' concept with a strict validation mode, plus streaming-safety fallbacks and clearer error semantics. Goals are: 1) ensure schema-validated outputs are enforced for non-streaming and streaming flows, 2) provide graceful fallback to deterministic non-strict outputs when partial streams cannot be reconciled, 3) keep OpenAI compatibility behavior stable for existing integrations. Summary of changes: - Add ResponseContract type and parser in server/response_contract/ (Go) that canonicalizes response_format definitions and compiles a lightweight validator used at both runtime and in the streaming layer. - Implement strict_mode flag on response_format: default off for backward compatibility; when on, server rejects final output that fails validation with structured error codes. - Streaming safety: streaming layer now buffers and validates schema-consistent JSON tokens as they arrive. If a stream contains irreversible partial output (ambiguous trailing token) the stream triggers an automatic graceful fallback: continue streaming with an explanatory structured warning event and final validation performed server-side; on strict_mode the request is marked failed and client receives structured error with validation details. - Tool/function-calling: function call responses are validated against function-defined output_contracts and tool results are re-validated when embedded into the main response. Added integration points so tool plugins can opt out for legacy tools. - OpenAI compatibility layer: maintain previous behavior by default. For API calls that set response_contract but also use the openai_compat flag, the compatibility layer forwards the response_contract and returns OpenAI-shaped error payloads when compatibility mode is requested. - Error model: introduce structured error codes: RESPONSE_CONTRACT_VIOLATION, STREAMING_AMBIGUOUS_STATE, TOOL_OUTPUT_MISMATCH. Each error includes a machine-friendly code and a human message. - Telemetry & observability: new metrics (response_contract.validation_failures, response_contract.stream_fallbacks) and traces tagged with contract_id and strict_mode. - Tests: added unit and integration tests for strict/non-strict, streaming fallback, tool-calling permutations, and openai_compat scenarios. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind a config flag response_contract.strict_mode in runtime config (default false). 2) Canary rollout to 5% traffic for 48h with alerting on validation_failures > 0.5% of requests; automatic rollback script included. 3) Enable for customers who opt-in via Console or API. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged; schema enforcement requires explicit response_contract in the request or customer opt-in. Known limitations: - Extremely large schemas (thousands of properties) have validation CPU cost; we include a budgeted short-circuit path that treats validation as async for very large schemas (results reported via post-check webhook) — documented in release notes. - Streaming buffer trades small extra latency for correctness; we tuned default buffer window to 150ms which we found acceptable in benchmarks. Related work items: Linear ENG-1428 (contract validation core), ENG-1499 (streaming safety), SUP-3312 (customer-reported tool mismatch). Checklist: - [x] Add runtime types and validator - [x] Streaming buffer + fallback path - [x] Tool/function calling validation hooks - [x] OpenAI compatibility mapping + error translation - [x] Metrics and tracing - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and console flag entry Observability and alerts: added Grafana panel reference (redwood/response-contract) and an alert rule for response_contract.validation_failures. Documentation: see docs/response-contract.md and SDK notes for Python/TS on shape of errors and opt-in flows.

feat(tools): validate tool/function outputs against declared output_contracts and add opt-out hooks

ci_checks: perf-bench: pass (150ms buffer adds ~6% p95 latency in microbench)
release_notes:
- Introduces response_contract with optional strict_mode for schema-validated structured outputs.
- Streaming safety: automatic fallback and explicit STREAMING_AMBIGUOUS_STATE error when streaming cannot maintain schema guarantees.
- Tool/function outputs are validated against declared output_contracts; new TOOL_OUTPUT_MISMATCH error code.
- OpenAI compatibility remains the default; setting openai_compat returns OpenAI-shaped validation errors.
- New telemetry: response_contract.validation_failures, response_contract.stream_fallbacks.
rollback_plan: Feature is gated. Rollback consists of disabling response_contract.strict_mode via central config and invoking deploy/rollout-scripts/response-contract-canary.sh to revert canary; alerting triggers automated revert if validation_failures spike.
notes: This PR aims to be conservative: strict_mode is opt-in. We will monitor validation_failures and tool mismatch rates during the canary window before recommending wide enablement.
